text.p: - European commissioner Hans van den Broek kicks off official visit to Slovenia on Thursday by meeting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
- Slovenian parliament on Wednesday agreed on a law restricting the use and advertising of tobacco products.
- Slovenia's basketball team Smelt Olimpija defeated Barcelona by 77-65 in the third round of the Euro-league on Wednesday in Ljubljana.
- Slovenia fulfils all requirements necessary for joining NATO, Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun told a news conference on Wednesday.
- Prime Minister Drnovsek met Ljubljana's Archbishop Alojzij Sustar on Wednesday to discuss relations between the state and the church.
- The first stage of the reconstruction of the border tunnel Ljubelj will cost Slovenia 250 million tolars ($1.8 million).
- Employees of metal company Litostroj said that they will go on strike next week unless they receive their salaries for August by the end of this week.
- Slovenian police offered 450,000 tolars ($3,285) award for any information on Maksimiljan Vollmeier, who is accused of ordering a bomb attack on a judge in the city of Miklavz last week.

- Miran Mejak, leader of Slovenia's succession negotiation group said that Slovenia will insist on its demand that all assets of former Yugoslav's central bank remain frozen, so they can be divided in a way agreed by all successor states.
